London, 26<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**The Obama administration task force** is likely to recommend more aid for struggling U.S. automakers, Sen. Carl Levin, D-Mich. said, and told reporters that “it is clear” any assistance would be tied to new conditions on restructuring.  The task force faces a March 31 deadline to determine whether GM and Chrysler are worthy of up to $22 billion in additional bailout funds.  It remains unclear how the task force overseen by the White House and Treasury Department would tailor a new bailout package. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**GM** has persuaded more than 6,000 United Auto Workers members to take buyouts, meeting internal company goals, and almost doubling a Barclays Capital estimate people familiar with the results said. The buyouts, about 10% of GM’s UAW workforce, may open slots for GM to hire workers for half the current union rate. 

_Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Head of Toyota, Katsuaki Watanabe,** said that industry-wide sales in the US for March looked set to be flat or worse than the weak results seen in February.  “Annualized sales in January and February were a little above 9 million, and we’re hearing that March will be about the same if not worse than February”. He said he could not tell when car sales would bottom out globally.  In Japan, Watanabe said Toyota was not planning any factory holidays from May and beyond, when the company hopes to keep daily output above 10,000 units.  Toyota has said its global production would hit a trough in Q1 09, during which it has idled factories for days and weeks at a time while selling cars from its bloated inventory.  The head of Japan’s steel industry lobby said on Wednesday he expected Japanese carmakers to finish bringing inventory to appropriate levels by June, indicating that production for Q2 09 would likely remain low. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Honda** said today that it will delay the start of a new auto factory in Japan again as the outlook for the recovery in auto demand remains unclear.  It has put off the start of a new auto factory in Yorii, Saitama Prefecture, north of Tokyo, until 2012 at the earliest. _Source:  The Wall Street Journal_ 

**South Korea** plans to cut new-vehicle purchase taxes by 70% from May to Dec for drivers replacing autos registered before 2000, to spur domestic sales. The government also intends to expand support for automakers’ R&D, help parts-makers become more competitive and aid auto-financing companies. The government also cut excise taxes on new vehicles by 30% in Dec to stem slumps at Hyundai, Kia and others.  2008 vehicle sales in South Korea may fall 8.7% to 1.05 million units, the lowest in five years. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Aquarius Platinum and Ridge Mining** announced that they expect to sign an implementation agreement in connection with Aquarius’ acquisition of Ridge prior to 27 March 2009.  Under the terms of the Implementation Agreement, Aquarius would agree t

o make an all share offer for the entire issued share capital of Ridge at an exchange ratio of 1 Aquarius share for every 2.75 Ridge shares.  At this exchange ratio the terms of the Acquisition value the entire existing issued and to be issued ordinary share capital of Ridge at about £63 million. This represents an implied price of 66.9 pence for each Ridge Share, based on 184.0 pence per Aquarius Share, being the closing price on the London Stock Exchange yesterday. 

_Source:  RTT News_ 

**Aquarius** announced its intention to raise up to ZAR650 million by way of a convertible bond issue. _Source: Yahoo Finance_
